Sierra Sharry and Lane Smith were expecting a baby in July. Sharry was eight months of pregnancy. But Smith fell and hit his head. He was taken to the hospital in Oklahoma City. He never recovered. Sharry wrote on Facebook, July 13th 214 was the the worst day of my life. I lost my best friend. The father of my unborn child. Their son Taos arrived a few weeks later. When it was time for his 6-month pictures, Sharry had a special request. Maybe the photographer could make their family complete, just for one picture.

People have strong opinions about Indiana’s new law regarding religious freedom. Some people are supporting companies that stop working in the state because they believe the law allows businesses to discriminate against gay people under the cover of religion. Others, like Indiana Governor Mike Pence, are surprised by the anger. and argue that the law is just like similar laws already in place in the federal government and 19 other states. The debate is intense because it involves both religious freedom and gay rights, and because people argue about what the law really means and why it was created.

Some fans of Lucille Ball want to remove a statue from a park in her hometown, Celoron, New York. They said that the statue is ugly and does not do justice to the star of "I Love Lucy." The life-size bronze statue has been compared to characters like the snake from "Beetlejuice" and actor Steve Buscemi, among other unflattering comparisons. Even Mayor Scott Schrecengost has gone on record saying he does not care for the statue, which shows the comic star holding a bottle of fictional nutrition elixir Vitameatavegamin. And yet, it has been a tourist draw since 2009 for Celoron, the comedian's birthplace, attracting visitors who pose with the statue for pictures.

Muhammadu Buhari was Nigeria’s leader once earlier, he came to power through a military coup. Now, he was elected by the vote. This election was one of the most intense in Nigeria’s history, and it is important for five reasons:

 For the first time in Nigeria’s history, the opposition party won the election against the party that was in power. Muhammadu Buhari, who is 72, won the Nigerian presidential election. he beat the current president, Goodluck Jonathan, by about two million votes. Nigeria is important because it is the biggest economy and most populous country in Africa; it is also one of Africa’s largest oil producers and is a major supplier of crude oil to the United States.

People online and in the streets were celebrating. It seemed like Iran had won the World Cup. But this was bigger. Young people waved flags from their sunroofs, played music loudly from their stereos, and chated online with the hashtag #IranTalks. The excitement came after a breakthrough nuclear deal with the United States and other world powers that promises to end Iran's international isolation under years of crippling sanctions. Just before midnight on Thursday, Vali Asr street, one of Tehran's main thoroughfares, turned into something like a block party. Car horns blared. Men danced in the middle of traffic. Some people flaunted U. dollar bills.

A federal court in Brooklyn has charged a fourth man, Dilkhayot Kasimov, with helping terrorists and supporting ISIS. Kasimov was added to a new legal document that builds on earlier charges against three other men: Abdurasul Hasanovich Juraboev, Akhror Saidakhmetov, and Abror Habibov. These three men already pleaded not guilty to two counts of providing support to a foreign terrorist group. Kasimov’s arrest status is unknown.

The third blood moon in a series was the shortest total lunar eclipse of the four. It was a good view for early risers in North America. The moon was fully in Earth's shadow from 4:58 a.m. Pacific Time (7:58 a.m. ET) on Saturday. This total eclipse lasted nearly five minutes. NASA says it is the shortest one of the century. The moon turned orange before, during, and after the total eclipse. This gives the moon the name "blood moon."

Istanbul, Turkey (CNN) – On Tuesday, many people in Turkey were worried. “What happened? Why can I get into the subway?” asked an elderly woman wearing a white head scarf and carrying several shopping bags. She was standing outside a blocked entrance to one of Istanbul’s busiest subway stations. She was among millions of Turks who were confused and worried by the worst power outage to hit the country in over a decade. Dozens of cities across Turkey lost power for hours on Tuesday. Millions of people were affected, including passengers stranded on paralyzed trains and subways.

During Holy Week, let us remind ourselves of what the Bible says about fair pay. The book of Isaiah 58.6 tells us that this is the kind of action God wants: to stop injustice, to end exploitation at work, to help those who are treated unfairly, to cancel debts. McDonald’s announcement that it will raise wages for 90,000 of its employees is a big win for fast-food workers and for all of us who support them. By standing together, fast-food workers are making it less acceptable for profitable companies like McDonald’s to pay wages so low that its workers are boxed into poverty.

California soon might be called the "Golden State" because its law are now yellow. Governor Jerry Brown on Wednesday made rules requiring everyone, including residents, businesses, and farms, to save water. He ordered cities and towns in the state, which is suffering from a severe drought, to cut their water use by 25%. Brown said, "We are in a new era." and added that the idea of having nice green law that uses lots of water every day is going to be a thing of the past. The 25% cut in water usage amounts to roughly 1.5 million acre-fe of water (an acre foot of water equals about 325,000 gallons) over the next nine months, state officials said.

It is time for British voters to decide who they will support. polling stations are opening across the UK for an election that could change the political system. This campaign is very short, especially compared to US standards, where candidates usually take years to prepare their messages. The election could result in the Conservative government, led by David Cameron, losing power to the Labour Party, led by Ed Miliband. or a chaotic situation where leaders try to form alliances with smaller parties. But all of this will only be known when the polls close late Thursday evening, local time.

This is the time of year when Christians around the world, more than 2 billion people, are thinking about the death and resurrection of Jesus. In memory of the tragic shooting of Christian college students in Kenya on Thursday, and given the ongoing danger to Christians in other countries, we are asking Christians during this Holy Week to also remember the suffering of believers. The death, bebeing, stoning, forced slavery, sexual abuse, human trafficking, harassment, bombing and displacement of hundreds of thousands of Christians – and others – whose faith alone has made them a target of religious extremists.

The exchanges between the city's top court clerk and two police officers were discovered during a U. s. Justice Department investigation of racial prejudice in the city's police and judicial system. The emails - which make offensive references to President Barack Obama, first lady Michelle Obama as well as Muslims and minorities - were obtained by the Washington Post on Thursday after a public records request. Two people, including a licensed greyhound trainer, have been arrested in Australia. They are charged in Queensland after the 55 dog carcasses were found dumped in the bush. according to Australian media reports. Two residents of Bundaberg, a 71-year-old man and a 64-year-old woman, were each charged with one count of unlawful possession of a firearm, broadcaster ABC reported. The woman, a licensed trainer, was also charged with obstructing police. Michael Beatty, spokesman for RSPCA Queensland, told ABC that inquiries are continuing. The animal rights organization is assisting Queensland police in their investigation.

Two years ago, Mike Premeau and Kathy Danke started a small business called Memories Gourmet Pizza Co. in their town in Wisconsin. They sold frozen pizzas, including breakfast pizzas and gluten-free options, in stores across Nichols, west of Green Bay. They built a loyal customer base. But this week, their business was threatened because people confused them with Memories Pizza of Walkerton, Indiana. That other business made national news after its owners said they would refuse to cater a same-sex wedding. People posted angry comments on Memories Gourmet Pizza’s Facebook page and called its phone number to protest.

A complete camel skeleton has been found under a cellar in Austria. The remains were uncovered by archaeologists from the University of Veterinary Medicine Vienna (Vetmeduni) while working on a shopping center in the city of Tulln in 2006-2007. The skeleton is thought to have been used by Ottoman troops during the siege of Vienna in the 17th century. "The partly excavated skeleton was at first suspected to be a large horse or cattle," archaeozoologist Alfred Galik said. "But one look at the cervical vertiae, the lower jaw and the metacarpal bones immediately revealed that this was a camel."

Andrew Getty, 47, and the grandson of J. Paul Getty, died on Tuesday in his Los Angeles home. His parents, Ann and Gordon Getty, issued a statement confirming the news. They asked members of the media and the public to respect the family's privacy during this difficult time. Ed Winter, assistant chief in the Los Angeles County coroner's office, told CNN affiliate KTLa that Getty's death "appe to be natural causes or an accident." Some medication had also been recovered from Getty's home, though investigators don't know if Getty was currently taking it or what his medical history was, Winter said.

We never will understand why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz crashed Germanwings Flight 9525 into the French Alps on March 24, killing everyone on board. The latest report shows that he sped up the descent of the plane to its doom. It's terrifying. As the investigation unfolds, we will learn more about to what extent Lubitz kept his mental illness secret, or how much help he sought. How much did his battle with depression affect his fitness to fly? Should he have walked away from his job? Should his doctors have sounded alarm bells? His case raises larger and important issues about people who are burdened with mental illness and the pressure of its stigma.

Prince Harry of Britain, who is 30 years, is going to spend some time with the Australian military. He arrives there on Monday for a four-week stay. The Australian Defence Forces said on Thursday that he will work and live with soldiers in several regiments in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth. He has already spent time with Australian troops on a number of occasions during his 10-year military career, a spokesman said.

Florida prison guards now are behind the bars. Two current and former corrections officers have been charged in a plot to kill a former inmate who was getting out of prison, the Florida Attorney General’s office said Thursday. An FBI informant met the men—Thomas Jordan Driver, 25; David Elliot Moran, 47; and Charles Thomas Newcomb, 42— after infiltrating a branch of the KKK: the Traditional American Knights of the Ku Klux Klan, CNN affiliate WJXT reported. Driver told the informant that he had gotten into a fight with the inmate and that he and Moran wanted him "six feet under," according to court documents.

Lausanne, Switzerland (CNN) – After a week of intense negotiations, world powers known as the P5+1 reached a framework agreement with Iran regarding its nuclear program. The success of this agreement is still uncertain. The parties have until the end of June to work out the details and put the plan to paper. But the talks this week were, nevertheless, historic, particularly for the otherwise frozen U.-Iranian relationship. But that's not to say they were glamorous. In fact, the negotiations this week provided a modern demonstration of diplomacy at its best, but also at its most hectic.

On Monday morning, an improvised bomb (made by terrorists) exploded near a United Nations vehicle near the Somali city of Garowe. The explosion killed six people, including four aid workers from UNICEF, the international children's agency. Somalia’s President said the attack was “an attack against the future of our country.” The attack happened about 8 a.m. in the administrative capital of the autonomous Puntland region, according to the United Nations Assistance Mission in Somalia. The terrorist group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for the attack. The attack follows a separate incident Sunday in which three African Union troops died in an ambush in the Lower Shabelle region of Somalia.

Prince Harry of Britain arrived in Australia on Monday. He will stay there for four weeks to working with the Australian military. Before he started his duties, the 30-year-old prince visited the Australian War Memorial in Canberra, the capital city. He paid his respects at the Tomb of the Unknown Australian Soldier. A crowd of people gathered outside the memorial. Some took photos of the royal visitor, while one boy held a sign celebrating the prince's hair color: "Red Heads Rule!" During his time down under, Harry "will work and live alongside colleagues in the Australian Army in a number of regiments in Sydney, Darwin and Perth," the Australian Defence Forces said last week.

Australia, a strong ally of the United States, has agreed to sharing some intelligence with Iran. Australian Foreign Minister Julie Bishop said the deal is an informal agreement, focused on tracking Australians who travel to Iraq to fight for ISIS. One Australian lawmaker reportedly called the move "dancing with the devil." Over the weekend, Bishop became the first Australian government minister to visit Iran in 12 years, meeting with President Hassan Rouhani. The intelligence-sharing deal was announced in an interview released Monday that Bishop gave to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation while in Tehran.

French investigators have said that the flight data recorder found from the crashed Germanwings Flight 9525 shows that co-pilot Andreas Lubitz intentionally used the controls to make the plane descend faster.

The recorder, known as the "black box," was found on Thursday by recovery teams who had been searching the mountainside in the French Alps for days since the March 24 crash. The BEA, the French air accident investigation agency, stated on Friday that its teams immediately began to examine the recorder's contents.

For a 110-day cat-and-mouse chase spanning from Antarctic waters to the coast of west Africa had an unlikely end when the crew of an alleged poaching vessel were rescued by conservationists pursuing them. Environmentalist group Sea Shepherd had been tailing the Thunder -- subject of an Interpol "purple notice" for suspected fraud and fisheries-related crimes -- since its ship the Bob Barker encountered it in the Southern Ocean several months ago. The pursuit ended early Monday in the Gulf of Guinea, off the coast of west Africa, when the Bob Barker received a distress call from the Thunder.

16-year-old Jason Zobott goes to Huntley High School in suburban Chicago. He arrive there around 7 a.m. every day. But his schedule is not normal for the rest of the day.

Jason is part of a special program at the school. This program mixes online lessons with regular classroom time. One third of the school’s 2,700 students are in this program. By 215, the school wants most students to join it.

Jason is a top student. He does many activities outside of school. He also has a lot of school work. He says, “Working online makes it easy to finish my tasks. I can learn by myself.”

Kenya launched airstrikes against the terrorist group Al-Shabaab in Somalia, after days of a deadly attack at Garissa University College in Kenya. A military source told CNN that these strikes were not about revenge for the Garissa massacre, which killed nearly 150 people. "The latest attack of Al-Shabaab bases by the Kenya military is part of the ongoing operations that started in 2111. It is not a retaliation to the Garissa attack. The operation has been ongoing," the military source said Monday. It is customary for Kenyan military sources not to give their names to media.

Pope Francis gave his traditional Easter speech, which called the "urbi et orbi" address (Latin for "to the city (Rome) and to the world"). He reminded the world that the Vatican is its own country and that he serves as a moral leader. He spoke about the suffering of people in current conflicts and asked for an end to violence everywhere. He specifically asked for the blood fighting to stop in Iraq and Syria and for humanitarian aid to reach those who need it. He said, "May the international community not stand by before the immense humanitarian tragedy unfolding in these countries and the drama of the numerous refugees."

D officials have asked anyone with information about the rope noose, which was found near a student center at 2 a.m., to call campus police. Photos of the noose prompted outrage from the community as they were passed along on social media. At a forum held on the steps of Duke Chapel, close to where the noose was hung, hundreds of people gathered. "You came here for the reason that you want to say with me, 'This is no Duke we will accept. This is no Duke we want. This is not the Duke we're here to experience.

Muhanad Mahmoud Al Farekh, 29, appeared in court on Thursday. He is a U.S. citizen who has alleged connections to al Qaeda. He did not plead guilty to charges of helping terrorists.

Al Farekh was sent from Pakistan to the United States. He is accused of planning to fight against American forces in other countries. This is stated in a legal document that was kept secret in a U U States District Court in Brooklyn, New York. CNN counterterrorism analyst Philip Mudd said, "This is news for celebration."

Saudi state media reported that a Saudi border guard was killed in a gun exchange with militants in Yemen. This is the first publicly known death of a Saudi soldier since Saudi Arabia started bombing rebel targets in its southern neighbor, Yemen. The fighting happened on Wednesday night at the border in the Asir region of southwestern Saudi Arabia. The Saudi Press Agency said that militants in a mountainous area in Yemen opened fire on Saudi border troops, who returned fire. The Saudi media outlet said that the slain border guard was identified as Cpl. Salman Ali Yahya al-Maliki. besides the slain border guard, 10 others suffered injuries that were not life-threatening.

I felt nervous because I was not the only person from the Gulf countries in the CNN team. People expected that I was familiar with camel racing, an ancient tradition in the region. But despite my attempts to dress in a kandora, a UAE national dress, my modern outlook on life means I am a total outsider in this world. A cheerful farm owner leads us inside the majlis - meeting area - where the camel owners are gathering. The wide space of the majlis feels like an ornate theater. The camel owners are sitting on the floor, eating the a'aish, a traditional Arabic dish of fish and rice, laid out in front of them. The conversation is loud and exciting.

He wants to talk about how for the first time he is thinking about leaving his safe place and going back to the United States.

Documents from CNN show that the Missouri National Guard used strong military language, such as "enemy forces" and "adversaries" to describe protesters when they was deployed to Ferguson, Missouri, last year. The protests happened sporly from August through the end of the year.

Gunmen attacked the Somalia’s education ministry in Mogadishu, the capital of Somalia, on Tuesday. This attack was a two-pronged attack that killed at least 12 people and injured 16 others, officials said. The Islamist militant group Al-Shabaab is responsible for the attack in the center of Mogadishu, group spokesman Abu Musab said. The attack began when two suicide bombers detonated their car at the entrance of the two-story building housing the Ministry of Education, Culture & Higher Education, Somali National Security Ministry spokesman Mohamed Yusuf said. Five gunmen then entered the building, shooting people inside, Yusuf said.

Gregory Margolin, now 87, was only 16 years when he fought in the Soviet Red Army during World II. His family fled from the Nazis. Margolin says, "I did not show that I was Jewish," but it did not matter because people were being killed left and right. All around me. This year, in Ukraine, he found himself again surrounded by war. Margolin was a sniper who rose to be a commander in the army. His old uniform is still adorned with medals from his time in the military. His granddaughter Liora still marvels at his stories from the war. She is amazed that he managed to survive.

How can more than 200 Nigerian schoolgirls disappear? And why does the Nigerian government and the world allow this to happen? It is now 365 days since the girls were taken from their boarding school dormitory in the early morning in Chibok, northeastern Nigeria. They are still missing. We should all feel ashamed: ashamed that we live in a world where the lives of young girls can be destroyed by violent criminals without punishment. ashamed that when such terrible acts happen, our attention fades so quickly.

Norway is going to stop broadcasting traditional FM radio. The country is scheduled to become the first in the world to phase out radio entirely. That doesn't mean that Norwegians will be left with radio silence; they'll merely have to tune in digitally. According to officials in Oslo, many in this nation of 5 million have already made the move. On FM, Norwegians can only find five stations. On the Digital Audio Broadcasting network, there are four times that number. Half the country already listens that way, said Culture Minister Thorhild Widvey.

Everyone is a favorite story about a comeback, especially one that is tiny. After its name was banned from science books for more than a century, a new study suggests that the Brontosaurus belongs to its own genus, and therefore deserves its own name. O.C. Marsh first named the Brontosaurus in 1879, after he received 25 crates of bones discovered at Como Bluff, Wyoming, according to the Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History. Similar to, though not as large as the Apatosaurus discovered a couple of years prior, Marsh named the dinosaur, "Brontosaurus," or "thunder lizard."

Al Qaeda has announced a reward in a conflict in Yemen. The group, called Al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula, offered anyone who killing or capturing two Shia Muslim leaders a reward of 20 kilograms of gold. This gold is worth about $774,000. The group wants the death or capture of Houthi leader Abdelmalik Bedrudin Al-Houthi and former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh. Al Qaeda calls these men "the two heads of evil." Al Qaeda is one of several groups fighting to control Yemen.

A white c sat at the front of New Shiloh Baptist Church in West Baltimore. A gospel choir sang for a large crowd gathered to honor Freddie Gray. A Saudi source told CNN that Saudi special forces helped Yemeni fighters fighting the Houthis and their allies in Aden. The source said that Saudi special forces were on the ground in non-combat roles "coordinating and guiding" the battle against Houthi forces and fighters loyal to former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh. Houthi rebels, meanwhile, withdrew from the presidential palace and other key parts of the southern port city of Aden following heavy Saudi airstrikes, according to the source. A Detroit mother, Mitchelle Angela Blair, was charged on Wednesday with murder and torture. Police arrested her last month after finding the bodies of two of her children inside a freezer.

Way County Prosecutor Kym Worthy says Blair killed her 13-year-old daughter, Stoni Ann Blair, and her 9-year-old son, Stephen Gage Berry.

Speaking to CNN from his Miami training base ahead of the April 25 showdown with American challenger Bryant Jennings in New York, Klitschko said the crisis in his homeland has left him shocked and upset. "My country is unfortunately suffering in the war with Russia -- not that Ukraine tried to give any aggression to any other nation, in this particular case Russia, unfortunately it's the other way around," Klitschko told CNN.

The Hatton Garden heist, as it will be likely be known, was every safe deposit box holder's nightmare, every movie director's dream. Thieves using heavy cutting equipment and rappelling gear broke into the vault of an esteemed 60-year-old safe deposit company in the heart of London over the past holiday weekend, possibly taking advantage of as many as four days to rifle through an uncounted number of safe deposit boxes. And they reportedly got away with hundreds of thousands of pounds worth of gems and cash -- even, in the educated guess of one former police official, as much as 200 million pounds, or $300 million.

As we approaching April 27, the day that South Africa marks the anniversary of the first post-apartheid elections held that day in 1994, we are faced with yet another wave of deadly attacks against African migrants. Outrage triggered by this violence is being heard loudly throughout social media with "#WeAreAfrica" showcasing the need for a common front against this affront. These recurring attacks against migrants and their property might be read as one more indication of how the rainbow nation's dream has faltered. In 1989, Iran’s leader, Ayatollah Khomeini, was accepting a ceasefire to end the war with Iraq. The war had helped define Khomeini's regime, the Islamic Republic, which he had founded a year before Saddam Hussein invaded Iran. Khomeini galvanized the nation, both his supporters and growing opponents, to fight against the enemy. He dragged out the war for eight years, despite Saddam's willingness to accept a ceasefire, and thus stabilized the foundations of the Islamic Republic. By the time he ended the war, the economy was in shambles, and there was no sign of his die-hard volunteers.

A deadly attack at Garissa University College in Kenya has nearly 150 people killed, including students, and many others wounded. Gunmen attacked the campus on Thursday morning while people were praying. They shot people randomly and took hostages before being killed by security forces, officials said. The U.S. Embassy in Nairobi said the Al-Shabaab militant group claimed responsibility. This attack comes just a few months after Al-Shabaab killed non-Muslim workers at a Kenyan quarry. The terrorist group has been responsible for many attacks in the region. It has also recruited some Americans, especially from the Somali-American community in Minnesota.

A university in South Africa has removed a statue of Cecil Rhodes, who was a British colonial leader. This happened after weeks of protests. University of Cape Town students started a campaign last month, using the hashtag #RhodesMustFall on social media to demand the statue be taken down. They argued that his history was marked by racism. Now, the hashtag is #RhodesHas Fallen. The university announced on Wednesday that the heritage authority gave them permission to remove the statue from the campus. The university stated in a release that these actions are being taken to ensure the safety of the statue while matters concerning its future are resolved.

The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights said this on Thursday. A year ago, the number was 162,402. The year before that, the United Nations said 70,000 people had died. Ailina Tsarnaeva appeared in Manhattan Criminal Court. She was quiet and seemed shy, but prosecutors says she was not shy when it came to a perceived rival. A Gaza police official told CNN that the door’s owner, Rabea Darduna, filed a complaint with a Gaza court. saying he sold the door for only 175 U. Dollars, not knowing it was valuable. The attacks against Houthi rebels in Yemen continue on Tuesday. The Saudi-led coalition forces have gaining more control, while many locals are fleeing the violence. The fighting has caused many deaths, including dozens of civilians.
